description: Three-phase power meter with split-core (EM-SC) or flexible-coil (EM-FC) current sensors, Modbus RTU: frequency, currents, voltages, power factors, status, cumulative energies and, on EM2 hardware with firmware 4.0 or later, 1 s and 60 s averages and per-phase energy counters
source: eTactica, EM -SC/FC Modbus Register Map, version 2.1 (2018-04-10)
notes: Modbus RTU on half-duplex RS485, 19200 baud, 8 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit by default (configurable from firmware 3.2 through register 0x2008). The Modbus unit ID defaults to the last byte of the serial number (for example 00.04.A3.ED.2B.D1 gives 0xD1) and can be changed in register 0x2009; the unit_id here is only a placeholder.
Functions 0x03 (read holding registers) and 0x10 (write multiple registers).
Addresses are the native register (PDU) addresses of the manual, address base 0: register 0x2000 is 8192 here, and 48192 in the manual's Modicon notation.

All values are big-endian, most significant byte first; 32-bit and 64-bit values are stored most significant register first. Registers are unsigned 16-bit unless the manual says otherwise; power factors are signed.

Power factor registers 0x201E to 0x2020 are given as value times 100 and the EM2 ones as value times 10000. A positive factor is active import and a negative one export; leading or lagging is given by the separate sign registers (-1 or 1).
The manual lists the energy counters in milli (0x2028, 0x202F) and micro (EM2) watt hours and var hours, as signed 64-bit values; the scale here converts them to Wh and varh.
The registers from 0x2100 are only on EM2 hardware with firmware 4.0 or later (marked with firmware_min); the registers up to 0x2032 are given for all EM devices.
Writing the serial settings, the slave ID or a counter takes effect after the command register 0x2006 is written with the store bit.

The status register is given as one flag per bit; any bit set makes the status LED blink faster. The manual's firmware version and product ID registers have no stated encoding, so they are given as raw numbers.
Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.
